subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this umbrella stay open until both high-frequency cron warnings and cron base-session retention semantics are resolved, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but the warning threshold and which cron base sessions are disposable are compatibility-sensitive product choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep Open For Linked Slices
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while maintainers review the warning path and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90194, then split only any leftovers.

options.title: Split Remaining Guardrails
options.body: Create or confirm narrower issues for context-threshold warnings, high-frequency warnings, and cleanup behavior so each PR closes only its own slice.

options.title: Reject Fixed Warning Threshold
options.body: If a fixed sub-30-minute advisory is not desired, close or narrow the warning PR path and keep retention cleanup as the primary bug path.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Linked Slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while maintainers review the warning path and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90194, then split only any leftovers.

likelyOwner.reason: The hardest unresolved decision is the cron/session lifecycle boundary around what the reaper may safely prune.
